subject: Clarify scope of output use, model training consent, and feedback license
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@prospectcorp.com>

Cc: procurement@prospectcorp.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines: Use rights + training consent (Order Form v2)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited. Attached are our redlines to the Order Form and a short note from Legal. There are three items blocking procurement sign-off:

1) Output ownership: we need an express right to own outputs derived from our data (including derivatives used in product).
2) Training/data use: we cannot give a broad permission to retrain models on our content; any training use needs explicit opt-in and scope limits.
3) Feedback license: we want confirmation that any feedback or telemetry you use for model improvements will be anonymized and limited to aggregated, non-attributable signals.

Can you share Redwood's position and proposed alternate language? Procurement is eager to get this wrapped by EOD Tuesday.

Attachments: ProspectCorp_redlines_annotated.pdf (PDF, 480KB)

Thanks,
Aisha Khan

Subject: Fwd: Redlines: Use rights + training consent (Order Form v2)

Laura / Ben — forwarding ProspectCorp's annotated redlines. High level ask: they want explicit output ownership, narrow/no training rights, and stronger guarantees on feedback telemetry.

Quick thoughts / questions for Legal (Laura):
- Output ownership: we usually grant customers a right to use outputs but avoid a broad assignment of title that could imply ownership of model weights. Can we propose: "Customer owns Customer Outputs; Redwood retains model weights and any generalized model improvements."
- Training: propose an opt-in checkbox on the Order Form and a limited-scope "learning data" carveout (explicitly excluding customer PII). Is that sufficient?
- Feedback license: suggest a time-bound, anonymized, aggregated feedback license for product quality improvements with an explicit opt-out.

Can you draft redline language we can send back today? Procurement wants a trackable doc (DocuSign) once legal agrees.

—Dylan
From: laura.bennett@redwood.com <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Redlines: Use rights + training consent (Order Form v2)

Dylan / Ben — reviewed ProspectCorp's annotations. I drafted candidate language and rationale below; attached is an annotated PDF that maps clauses to the redlines. High level: we need to protect model IP (weights/architecture) and our ability to improve models, but we can be explicit about customer outputs and provide a scoped feedback/license path.

Proposed redline snippets (Order Form / MSA):
1) Customer Outputs: "Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to Outputs generated solely from Customer Input (\"Customer Outputs\"). Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Customer Outputs for its business purposes."

Rationale: grants the customer's practical rights without implying transfer of model weights or training artifacts.

2) Training Use (Order Form opt-in): "Customer may elect to permit Redwood to use Customer Inputs and Customer Outputs for model training and improvement by executing the 'Training Consent' addendum on the Order Form. If elected, Redwood will process such data in accordance with the Training Addendum's scope and security controls; Customer may revoke consent with 60 days' notice for future processing."

Rationale: opt-in keeps procurement happy and gives us an avenue for post-deal training with explicit controls.

3) Feedback License (limited): "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, perpetual license to use feedback data that is de-identified and aggregated (\"Feedback Data\") for Redwood's internal quality improvement and model research purposes. Feedback Data shall not include Customer Personal Data or Customer Confidential Information."

Rationale: preserves our ability to learn from usage while addressing anonymization concerns. Consider adding a maximum retention period (e.g., 24 months) for Feedback Data to ease concerns.

I'll attach the annotated doc: ProspectCorp_redlines_annotated.pdf. If we like the wording, Ben can produce a tracked Order Form to send back.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposed compromise language re: outputs & training (Order Form v2)

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear redlines. Redwood's legal team reviewed and we think there is a straightforward compromise that should keep procurement moving: below are the exact clauses we'd like to propose for the Order Form / MSA.

1) Customer Outputs: Customer retains all right, title and interest in Outputs generated solely from Customer Inputs. Redwood confirms it will not assert ownership over Customer Outputs.

2) Training Consent (opt-in): We will add an explicit checkbox on the Order Form labeled 'Training Consent'. If Customer checks this box, Redwood may use Customer Inputs and Customer Outputs for model training under a separate Training Addendum that specifies: a) scope of use, b) anonymization/pseudonymization steps, c) security controls, and d) revocation mechanics (60-day notice for cessation of new training). If the box is left unchecked, Redwood will not use Customer Inputs/Outputs for training.

3) Feedback License (anonymized & time-limited): Customer grants a limited license to use de-identified, aggregated feedback data for product improvements for a period not to exceed 24 months from collection. Feedback will exclude Customer Personal Data and be retained only for the stated purpose. Customers can opt-out of Feedback Collection entirely via a control in the Console.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to produce a tracked Order Form (I asked him to start).
- Laura to attach the annotated redline pdf (done).
- I will upload the tracked doc to DocuSign and share the link with your procurement team.

If that sounds acceptable, I'll send the tracked Order Form by EOD Monday.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
